Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, some of which appear to have cavitation or central necrosis (particularly the large nodule in the right lower zone). In a patient presenting with chest pain and non-productive cough, this radiographic pattern of multiple necrotizing nodules is highly characteristic of Necrotizing Sarcoid Granulomatosis (NSG), a rare variant of sarcoidosis that mimics vasculitis or malignancy but fits the specific "necrotizing" descriptor often tested with this image.
